title: Partner/steward outreach + candidate dataset shortlist + requestor contact
context: The Hee-Lee Oss 'delivered, not merged' bar requires that at least one named partner/steward has adopted, hosted, cited, or formally requested a reanalysis. At project start, no steward is secured and verifiedNeed is false for all tasks. Partner/steward outreach is a hard M0/M1 objective — without it the project cannot declare itself shipped. Candidate stewards include the EMBL-EBI PRIDE team, nf-core/proteomics community, cancer-data consortia using open data, and original dataset authors. A candidate dataset shortlist is also needed so the pilot triage task (gate-pilot-008) has a ranked set to work from.
objective: Conduct outreach to candidate partner/steward organizations, produce a shortlist of candidate open PRIDE cancer datasets suitable for the first reanalysis, and log at least one initial contact with a potential requestor (dataset author, curator, or reproducibility initiative).
acceptanceCriteria: A shortlist of at least 3 candidate open PRIDE/ProteomeXchange cancer datasets is documented, each with: accession, repository, rough dataset size, acquisition type (DDA/DIA), and a suitability note for donated-session budget.
At least one outreach thread with a potential partner or steward (e.g., PRIDE team, nf-core/proteomics, a dataset author, or a reproducibility initiative) is opened and its status logged.
At least one candidate requestor (dataset author, curator, or steward) has been contacted and the contact is recorded.
The outreach and shortlist document is committed to the project repo, licensed CC-BY-4.0, and clearly states that verifiedNeed remains false until a named partner confirms adoption/citation/request.
resources: PLAN.md — Problem & beneficiaries, Partner org section
PRIDE Archive / ProteomeXchange — open cancer proteomics dataset listings
output: A committed outreach log and candidate dataset shortlist document recording partner contacts, candidate datasets, and the current outreach status; licensed CC-BY-4.0.
